subject: Private hosting discovery — constraints, priority gaps, next owners
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@blueseedhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting discovery — constraints, priority gaps, next owners

Hi Maria — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Call highlights / pain points (as you described):
- Data residency: all PHI and audit logs must remain in the customer VPC in us-west-2; no copy to managed storage outside your account.
- Network restrictions: outbound-only egress limited to a small whitelist, strict egress filtering via a corporate proxy, no inbound public IPs allowed.
- Air-gap/regulatory driver: procurement requires an air-gapped option for high-risk workflows and evidence for annual audit (SOC2/HIPAA).
- Key management: keys must be customer-controlled (HSM/KMS in their VPC) and we cannot hold plaintext keys.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile <180ms for user-facing RL prompts is desired; heavier batch workloads can be lower priority.

Goals you stated: POC in 8–10 weeks focusing on inference correctness and isolation; security signoff in second procurement gate; a cost target that keeps per-API-call economics close to public-hosted for common inference paths.

Immediate asks / owners:
1) Jordan: share a concise residency & hosting summary + MOP outline (attached: redwood-residency-summary.pdf, initial-mop-outline.docx). ACTION: shared now.
2) Laura: coordinate a 90-minute technical deep-dive next week with your infra/security SME and our infra engineer (Ben). ACTION: @laura_bennett to propose times.
3) Maria / Blueseed: send the internal security questionnaire and any existing network diagrams (we called out the need for a clear picture of outbound proxy/egress rules). ACTION: Maria to share VPC/network diagram + compliance owner contacts.

Open technical risks we flagged:
- If outbound is only allowed to a proxy that terminates TLS, we need clarity on mutual TLS and certificate injectability.
- HSM integration path: we can support customer-managed KMS but need service account access patterns defined for key retrieval.
- Air-gap option timeline & acceptance criteria need to be defined now (what "air-gapped" means for Blueseed: fully isolated compute with controlled data bridges vs periodic physical media exchange?).

Next concrete steps:
- Laura to send three slot options for the tech deep-dive by EOD today.
- Maria to upload the network diagram + questionnaire responses to the Drive link below by EOD Thursday.
- Ben to prepare a short checklist of ports/protocols and per-component persistence behaviors (we'll include that in the deep-dive agenda).

Links & attachments: Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-blueseed-precall
Attachments: redwood-residency-summary.pdf (stub), initial-mop-outline.docx (stub), requested-network-checklist.xlsx (stub)

Thanks — I included Laura and Ben to quickly pull ops/eng alignment. If any of this is misremembered or missing, let me know and I'll correct.

—Jordan

Thanks Jordan — good summary, appreciate it. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Our outbound policy is very strict: only whitelisted destination IPs are allowed and everything must go through our corporate proxy (we cannot terminate TLS at the proxy for workloads that handle PHI). We will provide the IP ranges but expect them to be narrow.
- Procurement will need a one-page security evidence brief (SOC2 scope, data flow diagram, and the HSM integration approach).
- The air-gap ask is specific to our clinical trial workflows. For the POC we'd accept a logically isolated deployment in our VPC with no internet egress except to whitelisted Redwood endpoints; longer term they may ask for a physically isolated deployment.

I've copied our security lead (security@blueseedhealth.com) and will upload the network diagram and an early version of the questionnaire to the Drive by Thursday COB. We're targeting an internal review next Tuesday which is why the 8–10 week POC window looks reasonable.

Proposed availability for the deep-dive: Mon 6/22 10:00–11:30 PT or Tue 6/23 13:00–14:30 PT. Please confirm.

Thanks — I can take the 6/22 10:00–11:30 PT slot. Quick technical notes I'm attaching as a stub and dropping inline items we should confirm before the deep-dive: requested-network-checklist.xlsx (stub)

Preliminary ports/protocols + notes:
- Outbound HTTPS (443) required to whitelisted Redwood egress IPs. We can support mTLS but need the intermediary proxy to pass client certs or allow TLS passthrough for mutual auth.
- NTP outbound allowed for time sync.
- No inbound public IPs; all communication initiated from inside the VPC to Redwood-controlled endpoints.
- Persistent KV cache: by default our runtime keeps KV in RAM; optional disk-backed persistence needs explicit config and customer-managed storage. For air-gap POCs we recommend RAM-only with periodic snapshot exports to the customer's secure bucket.
- KMS: we support customer-owned KMS via IAM role assumption. For HSM we need a key-access pattern (API endpoint in customer VPC or AWS CloudHSM accessible from the subnet).

Acceptance criteria suggestions for the POC:
- Successful inference calls from a test app in Blueseed VPC with 95th percentile latency <250ms for the chosen prompt set.
- Demonstrated key rotation with customer KMS and no plaintext key exposure in Redwood logs.
- Evidence brief containing data flow diagram + SOC2 mappings for the components used.

I'll upload the one-page ports checklist and a short procurement evidence template to the Drive in 2 hours. Linking HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company.com/deal/DEAL-9876 — please log notes there after the call.

—Ben
